code.source:
marks = []
for n in range(3):
    marks.append(int(input("Mark: ")))
print("Marks:", marks)
print("Highest:", max(marks))
print("Average:", round(sum(marks) / len(marks), 1))

code.source:
marks = [72, 35, 90, 28, 64]
passed = 0
for m in marks:
    if m >= 40:
        passed = passed + 1
print("Passed:", passed, "of", len(marks))
print("Top:", max(marks), "Lowest:", min(marks))

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: average of an empty list
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the Python error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. The list is empty, so len is zero. The sum is zero, and dividing by zero is a zero division error. Python says, division by zero. Check the list first. An empty list counts as False, so a plain if marks does the job. Then print a friendly message instead of crashing.

props.error:
File "tracker.py", line 2, in <module>
    print(sum(marks) / len(marks))
          ~~~~~~~~~~~^~~~~~~~~~~~
ZeroDivisionError: division by zero
props.why: An empty list has length zero, and dividing by zero raises an error; test the list before you divide.

shorts.title: The tracker plan
shorts.script: Let us build a marks tracker. Start with an empty list. A loop asks for three marks, and appends each one. Then we print the whole list, the highest mark with max, and the average with sum divided by len. It uses the loop, the list, and the built in functions you already know. Plan on paper first, then type it. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Our second project.

shorts.title: Max, min, sum, len
shorts.hook: "Four built in functions do the heavy work on a list of numbers."
shorts.script: Four built in functions do the heavy work on a list of numbers. Max gives the biggest. Min gives the smallest. Sum adds everything. Len counts the items. Sum divided by len is the average. You do not need a loop for any of them. Learn these four, and a list of marks becomes a mini report in four lines. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Four helpers.

shorts.title: Count the passes
shorts.script: To count passes, use a counter. Start at zero. Loop over the marks. If a mark is forty or more, add one. After the loop, the counter says how many passed. Pair it with len, and you can print, passed three of five. This is the same counter pattern from the loop patterns episode, now on a list. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: A counter on a list.

shorts.title: Divide by zero
shorts.hook: "Here is the bug that crashes trackers."
shorts.script: Here is the bug that crashes trackers. The list is empty, so len is zero. Sum divided by len is a division by zero, and Python raises a zero division error. Check the list first. An empty list counts as False, so a simple if marks is enough. Then print a friendly message, and the program survives. Then run it, and compare with what you predicted. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Guard the average.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: "Why did the marks tracker get top marks?"
shorts.script: Why did the marks tracker get top marks? It always added up. Your challenge. Take the pass counter program, and extend it. Also print how many marks are below forty. You can count them with a second counter, or subtract the passes from the length. Which way is shorter? Post your improved version in the comments below, and show your output. Keep coding, says Xecxec! Full video: EP 32.
shorts.caption: Extend the tracker.
